explanation: I found no Mathlib declaration that states this result. The statement is built on the library's own `la_coord`, a coordinate map `K ⊗[ℚ] S →ₗ[ℚ] S` defined with `TensorProduct.lift` from `b.coord i`. It says that `t` lies in the additive subgroup generated by the pure tensors `z ⊗ s`, with `z` in the ℤ-span of the basis `b` and `s` in the subring `R`, exactly when every coordinate of `t` lies in `R`. Mathlib has the basic ingredients: `AddSubgroup.closure_le`, `AddSubgroup.sum_mem` and tensor-product bases such as `Algebra.TensorProduct.basis`. I know of no Mathlib result describing this integral-lattice-times-subring closure through its coordinates. I only checked the library's own `la_coord` and `la_sum_tmul_coord`; I did not run name or content searches in Mathlib. The proof itself only uses generic closure and sum lemmas together with the library's own lemmas.
